title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X/S is a smooth relative curve. P_{X/S} is the étale sheaf on X of étale maps (local 'uniformizers') X -> P^1_S. H_S = Aut_S(P^1_S) = PGL_2. The previous page defined, for two such étale maps t, s, a quadratic differential c(t,s) in Γ(X, ω_{X/S}^{⊗2}). Up to a normalization constant this is the algebraic Schwarzian derivative of s with respect to t. The next page writes it as 12·G_0 with G_0 = -D^{(3)}_t s/D^{(1)}_t s + (D^{(2)}_t s/D^{(1)}_t s)^2, using divided-power derivatives. Since D^{(2)} = s''/2 and D^{(3)} = s'''/6, one gets G_0 = -(1/6)·Schwarzian, so 12·G_0 = -2·Schwarzian.

This page formalises the properties of c and draws the consequences.
(1) Invariance under f^{-1}(H_S): c(g·s, g'·t) = c(s,t) for local sections s, t of P_X over an étale U -> X lying over an étale V -> S, and g, g' in H(V).
(2) Cocycle identity: c(s,t) + c(t,v) = c(s,v).
(3) Consequence: a 1-cocycle with values in a sheaf of groups, from a sheaf that is locally non-empty, defines a torsor. So one gets the étale sheaf Conn_{X/S} of relative projective connections on X/S. It is a torsor under ω_{X/S}^{⊗2}, with a canonical map c^X : P_{X/S} -> Conn_{X/S} such that c(t,s) = c^X(s) - c^X(t).
(4) P_{X/S}, Conn_{X/S} and c^X are formed compatibly with étale localisation. Hence c^X(t) = t^*(c), where c is the unique projective connection on P^1_S. It is unique because H^0(P^1, ω^{⊗2}) = 0, as on the previous page.
(5) Generalisation: replace P^1_S by any P^1-bundle (Brauer–Severi curve, conic bundle) X_0/S carrying a unique projective connection c_{X_0}. Then define c(t,s) = s^*(c_{X_0}) - t^*(c_{X_0}) for étale maps t, s : X -> X_0, with the analogous invariance and cocycle properties.

Purpose. This is the algebraic, arbitrary-base set-up for projective structures and projective connections on curves (uniformisation, Picard–Fuchs and Schwarzian equations). The next page leads to two points:
- Injectivity of P_X/H -> Conn in characteristic 0. Connections in the image are called 'intégrable par fonctions algébriques'.
- In characteristic p, invariance under Frobenius-twisted PGL_2, a refined torsor Conn_0 that avoids the factor 12, and the problem in characteristics 2 and 3.
errors: Sign and order conventions shift slightly: the invariance is written c(g·s, g'·t) = c(s,t) and the cocycle c(s,t)+c(t,v) = c(s,v), which forces c(s,t) = φ(t) - φ(s). The formula c(t,s) = c^X(s) - c^X(t) is consistent with this, so there is no real error.

The hypothesis 's'il y a une unique connexion' for a P^1-bundle X_0 is superfluous. Étale-locally X_0 ≅ P^1_S and the canonical connection there is PGL_2-invariant and unique, so it descends. Every Brauer–Severi curve over S therefore carries a unique projective connection.

The torsor Conn_{X/S} built from c (which carries the factor 12) degenerates when 12 is not invertible on S, i.e. in residue characteristics 2 and 3. Grothendieck repairs this on the next page with Conn_0; on this page the construction is implicitly only good for 6 invertible.

ideas.what: Schwarzian-type quadratic differential c(t,s) between two étale coordinates, PGL_2-invariant and satisfying a cocycle identity
ideas.modern_name: algebraic Schwarzian derivative as a PGL_2-invariant 1-cocycle
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Schwarz, Cayley); algebraic version in positive characteristic by Ihara (1974, 'Schwarzian equations'), later Mochizuki

ideas.what: Sheaf of relative projective connections as an ω^{⊗2}-torsor, constructed from the cocycle, with canonical map from étale coordinates
ideas.modern_name: torsor of projective connections / sl_2-opers over a relative curve; projective structures map to it

ideas.what: c^X(t) = t^*(canonical projective connection on P^1_S)
ideas.modern_name: pullback of the canonical projective structure on P^1 along étale charts

ideas.what: Replacing P^1_S by a twisted form (P^1-bundle) X_0 with its unique projective connection
ideas.modern_name: projective structures modelled on Brauer–Severi curves / twisted PGL_2-torsors
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in opers over non-trivial bases

missed.claim: This is an early (c. 1972) Grothendieck treatment of projective connections on relative curves over an arbitrary base S, as an étale torsor under ω^{⊗2} with a canonical map from étale coordinates. Together with the next page it addresses characteristic p (Frobenius-twisted PGL_2 invariance) and the factor 12, the problem at 2 and 3. It anticipates Ihara's 1974 work and Mochizuki's p-adic theory, but this page itself contains only the formal set-up.
missed.quote: le faisceau (ét) Conn_{X/S} des connexions ... relatives sur X rel. S, qui est un torseur sous ω^{⊗2}_{X/S}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority only: it documents Grothendieck's interest in projective structures and Schwarzian equations in mixed characteristic, a theme later central to Ihara and to Mochizuki's indigenous bundles and dormant opers.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is standard: the Schwarzian cocycle, the torsor of projective connections, and pullback from P^1. The only interest is historical, a scheme-theoretic, arbitrary-base formulation predating the published characteristic-p literature. The genuinely characteristic-p material is on the next page.
transcription_corrections: 'c^X_?(s)' should read c^X(s): c(t,s) = c^X(s) - c^X(t).
'connexions [?] P^1-[?] relatives' most likely reads 'connexions projectives relatives'; likewise 'une unique connexion projective c_{X_0}'.
After the diagram, 'où ,' introduces the diagram: U -> X and V -> S étale, with U lying over V.
'Conn_{X/S}' is written 'Conn' (abbreviation of connexions) in the manuscript.
'commute à la localisation' is likely 'commute à la localisation (étale)'.
